sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Professor C.T.
sentences.zh: C.T.温特教授

sentences.en: Nguyen teaches philosophy at the University of Utah,
sentences.zh: 在犹他大学教授哲学，

sentences.en: and he says the reason he got into this field is because he is drawn to life's big questions.
sentences.zh: 他说他进入这个领域的原因，是因为他被人生中的重大问题所吸引。

sentences.en: These weird, romantic, bizarre questions, like, about the meaning of life,
sentences.zh: 那些古怪、浪漫、离奇的问题，比如关于生命的意义，

sentences.en: and what is art for, like, are we just wasting our time doing our dumb hobbies,
sentences.zh: 以及艺术的目的是什么，比如我们是在浪费时间做那些愚蠢的爱好，

sentences.en: or is it the best part of life?
sentences.zh: 还是说这才是生命中最美好的部分？

sentences.en: Those were the questions I cared about.
sentences.zh: 那些才是我关心的问题。

sentences.en: But when he started teaching philosophy,
sentences.zh: 但当他开始教哲学时，

sentences.en: T.
sentences.zh: 温特

sentences.en: learned that what makes a good philosopher at a prestigious school
sentences.zh: 了解到在名校里，什么才算是一个优秀的哲学家，

sentences.en: had less to do with pursuing curiosity and had more to do with metrics.
sentences.zh: 这与追求好奇心关系不大，而与指标关系更大。

sentences.en: Your value as a philosopher seemed based on whether your papers were getting published
sentences.zh: 你作为哲学家的价值，似乎取决于你的论文是否发表在

sentences.en: in highly ranked philosophy journals.
sentences.zh: 高排名的哲学期刊上。

sentences.en: There's no moment where anyone told me to care about it,
sentences.zh: 没有人明确告诉过我要去在意这些，

sentences.en: but everybody just talks in that language,
sentences.zh: 但每个人都在用那种语言交流，

sentences.en: and suddenly you just find yourself kind of automatically thinking
sentences.zh: 突然间，你会发现自己不知不觉地认为，

sentences.en: that your goal is to publish in the top-ranked journals,
sentences.zh: 你的目标就是要在顶级期刊上发表文章，

sentences.en: and that that's what success means in philosophy.
sentences.zh: 而这就是哲学领域所谓的成功。

sentences.en: Suddenly, all the joy was sucked out of this thing that he loved so much.
sentences.zh: 刹那间，他所热爱的事物中所有的乐趣都被抽干了。

sentences.en: I was so bored with what I was writing because I was trying to go up this liSt.
sentences.zh: 我对自己的写作感到非常厌倦，因为我一直在试图攀登那份榜单。

sentences.en: It's so miserable that I was going to quit the profession
sentences.zh: 那种感觉太痛苦了，以至于我打算放弃这个职业，

sentences.en: after, like, having burned 10 years in it.
sentences.zh: 尽管我已经在这个领域投入了10年。

sentences.en: Instead of giving up, T.
sentences.zh: 温特没有选择放弃，

sentences.en: decided to do something that seemed like career suicide.
sentences.zh: 而是决定做一件看起来像是职业自杀的事情。

sentences.en: He threw out those metrics of success and went after something harder to measure,
sentences.zh: 他抛弃了那些成功的指标，转而追求更难衡量的事物，

sentences.en: his own curiosity.
sentences.zh: 即他自己的好奇心。

sentences.en: This is the story C.T.
sentences.zh: 这就是C.T.温特

sentences.en: Wendt uses to open his latest book,
sentences.zh: 在开篇讲述的故事，出自他的最新著作，

sentences.en: The Score, How to Stop Playing Someone Else's Game.
sentences.zh: 《得分：如何停止玩别人的游戏》。

sentences.en: In it, T.
sentences.zh: 在书中，温特

sentences.en: expands the definition of games to encompass all the ways
sentences.zh: 扩展了游戏的定义，涵盖了所有

sentences.en: metrics and scoring systems play out in our lives for good and for ill,
sentences.zh: 指标和评分系统在我们的生活中产生影响的方式，无论好坏，

sentences.en: from those dreaded philosophy journal rankings,
sentences.zh: 从那些令人恐惧的哲学期刊排名，

sentences.en: to Duolingo, Step Counting, and beyond.
sentences.zh: 到多邻国、步数统计等等。

sentences.en: I love this book, and I was so excited to talk to T.
sentences.zh: 我非常喜欢这本书，也很高兴能和温特

sentences.en: about it.
sentences.zh: 谈论它。

sentences.en: We had a delightfully meandering conversation about the philosophy of games,
sentences.zh: 我们进行了一场令人愉悦且漫无边际的对话，探讨了游戏哲学、

sentences.en: the trap of metrics, and how to make sure we're playing the game we want to be playing.
sentences.zh: 指标的陷阱，以及如何确保我们玩的是自己想玩的游戏。

sentences.en: Our chat started with me asking T.
sentences.zh: 我们的谈话始于我请温特

sentences.en: to define a concept he coined called value capture.
sentences.zh: 定义他创造的一个概念：价值捕获。

sentences.en: Value capture is what happens when your own values are rich or subtle
sentences.zh: 价值捕获是指，当你的个人价值观丰富、微妙，

sentences.en: or developing in that direction, and then you get put in a social setting,
sentences.zh: 或者正朝着那个方向发展时，你被置于一种社会环境、

sentences.en: an institution or with a technology that feeds you simplified,
sentences.zh: 一种机构或一种技术之中，它为你提供的是简化后的、

sentences.en: typically quantified versions of your values,
sentences.zh: 通常是量化版本的价值观，

sentences.en: and then the simplified versions take over.
sentences.zh: 然后这些简化版本就会占据主导地位。

sentences.en: You have been here.
sentences.zh: 你一定经历过这种情况。

sentences.en: You have been value captured.
sentences.zh: 你已经被价值捕获了。

sentences.en: It happens all the time.
sentences.zh: 这种情况时有发生。

sentences.en: Maybe you start going to school because you want to learn,
sentences.zh: 也许你开始上学是因为你想学习，

sentences.en: or you start walking more for your health,
sentences.zh: 或者你开始多走路是为了健康，

sentences.en: but then you get focused on a metric,
sentences.zh: 但后来你开始关注一个指标，

sentences.en: like getting all A's or counting steps,
sentences.zh: 比如拿到全A或者计算步数，

sentences.en: and suddenly you're very far from the values that drove you to do those things in the first place.
sentences.zh: 突然间，你离最初驱使你做这些事情的价值观已经非常遥远了。

sentences.en: This kind of dynamic is everywhere.
sentences.zh: 这种动态无处不在。

sentences.en: One of my favorite examples.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的例子之一。

sentences.en: A lot of these things are so insidious that I hadn't realized the degree to which I internalized this,
sentences.zh: 很多这类事情非常隐蔽，以至于我都没有意识到自己内化到了什么程度，

sentences.en: and I've been working on this stuff for like five years,
sentences.zh: 尽管我研究这些东西已经五年了，

sentences.en: and I was sitting there watching my kid being like,
sentences.zh: 我坐在那里看着我的孩子，心想，

sentences.en: you know, I should reduce his screen time.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我应该减少他的屏幕时间。

sentences.en: So screen time is a massive metric for a lot of us.
sentences.zh: 所以屏幕时间对我们很多人来说是一个巨大的指标。

sentences.en: But then if you think about it, it's a crap metric.
sentences.zh: 但如果你仔细想想，这是一个糟糕的指标。

sentences.en: One week, my screen time skyrocketed.
sentences.zh: 有一周，我的屏幕时间飙升了。

sentences.en: The reason my screen time skyrocketed was I was reading two different translations of Kant on my iPad, right?
sentences.zh: 屏幕时间飙升的原因是我在iPad上阅读康德的两种不同译本，对吧？

sentences.en: That's not – that is not a bad thing for me to do.
sentences.zh: 这并不是——对我来说，这不是一件坏事。

sentences.en: But I was watching my kid.
sentences.zh: 但我看着我的孩子，

sentences.en: I'm like, oh, I'm supposed to reduce his screen time.
sentences.zh: 心想，哦，我应该减少他的屏幕时间。

sentences.en: And one of the things I noticed is that sometimes when he's on his screen,
sentences.zh: 我注意到的一件事是，有时当他在看屏幕时，

sentences.en: he's watching the dumbest possible ASMR videos.
sentences.zh: 他看的是最愚蠢的ASMR视频。

sentences.en: Sometimes he is literally learning geopolitics.
sentences.zh: 有时他确实是在学习地缘政治。

sentences.en: He's obsessed with videos that explain the history of the rise of World War I and World War II.
sentences.zh: 他沉迷于那些解释第一次世界大战和第二次世界大战起因的视频。

sentences.en: He's nine.
sentences.zh: 他才九岁。

sentences.en: Sometimes he is playing dumb clicker games.
sentences.zh: 有时他在玩愚蠢的点击游戏。

sentences.en: Sometimes he's building architectural masterpieces in Minecraft with like coded logic gates.
sentences.zh: 有时他用Minecraft里的编码逻辑门建造建筑杰作。

sentences.en: These are not the same thing, right?
sentences.zh: 这些东西并不一样，对吧？

sentences.en: There's no way in which these are valuable in anything like the same amount.
sentences.zh: 它们在任何意义上都不具备相同的价值。

sentences.en: But it's very easy for a device to capture screen time.
sentences.zh: 但设备很容易捕捉到屏幕时间。

sentences.en: And I think this is part of my core worry here is that we're outsourcing our values to an external product or institution.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是我核心担忧的一部分，即我们将价值观外包给了外部产品或机构。

sentences.en: And sometimes that's a classical story of evil.
sentences.zh: 有时这是一个经典的邪恶故事。

sentences.en: Somebody like some Machiavellian tells us what to value.
sentences.zh: 某个马基雅维利式的人物告诉我们该重视什么。

sentences.en: But a lot of the times, like a lot of outsourcing, what we're outsourcing it to is a process that's convenient at scale.
sentences.zh: 但很多时候，就像许多外包一样，我们外包给的是一个在大规模应用下很方便的流程。

sentences.en: What's determining how a lot of us parent is just that screen time happens to be an easy thing for our devices to measure automatically without any particular input from us.
sentences.zh: 决定我们很多人育儿方式的，仅仅是因为屏幕时间恰好是我们的设备无需我们输入任何信息就能自动测量的简单事物。

sentences.en: T says that forcing the things we value into the sausage grinder of metrics can often flatten nuance and meaning in favor of generating a value that's more simple and measurable.
sentences.zh: 温特说，将我们重视的事物强行塞进指标的绞肉机中，往往会抹平细微差别和意义，转而生成一种更简单、可衡量的价值。

sentences.en: It is and often feels awful and reductive.
sentences.zh: 这确实让人感觉糟糕且具有还原性。

sentences.en: And yet we can't help being seduced by it.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们却无法抗拒它的诱惑。

sentences.en: Why do you think it is that that you and others actually find this kind of value capture framework so tempting and rewarding enough that that you that pulls you into this type of engagement?
sentences.zh: 你认为为什么你和其他人会觉得这种价值捕获框架如此诱人且具有足够的奖励性，以至于让你陷入这种参与模式？

sentences.en: I mean, life is full of these complicated existential value clashes where you have to make these nauseating decisions.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，生活充满了这些复杂的生存价值冲突，你必须做出那些令人作呕的决定。

sentences.en: I mean,
sentences.zh: 我是说，

sentences.en: I think every day I'm faced with the decision of whether to spend more time playing with my kids or more time doing hobbies I enjoy or more time like staying up late doing extra email.
sentences.zh: 我想我每天都面临着一个决定：是花更多时间陪孩子玩，还是花更多时间做我喜欢的爱好，或者是熬夜处理额外的邮件。

sentences.en: That's a terrifying decision that like asks me to weigh these very different values.
sentences.zh: 那是一个可怕的决定，要求我权衡这些截然不同的价值观。

sentences.en: But if you automate it, if you decide there's only one thing that's important and that everything feeds into that thing in a mechanically measurable way,
sentences.zh: 但如果你将其自动化，如果你认定只有一件事是重要的，并且一切都以一种机械可衡量的方式服务于那件事，

sentences.en: suddenly you're sheltered from the existential storm.
sentences.zh: 突然间，你就从生存的风暴中得到了庇护。

sentences.en: You're safe.
sentences.zh: 你是安全的。

sentences.en: So that's one answer.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个答案。

sentences.en: The second answer is the seductiveness is making yourself comprehensible and communicable to other people.
sentences.zh: 第二个答案是，这种诱惑力在于让你自己变得容易被他人理解和交流。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: Like when I – I mean this is something I do – I have done and I'm very embarrassed about.
sentences.zh: 就像我——我是说这是我做过的事情——我做过，而且对此感到非常尴尬。

sentences.en: So, you know, while I was researching this book and looking at scoring systems, I started reading about yo-yo and I got really into yo-yoing.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，当我在研究这本书并查看评分系统时，我开始阅读关于悠悠球的内容，然后我真的迷上了玩悠悠球。

sentences.en: Yo-yoing is super interesting.
sentences.zh: 玩悠悠球超级有趣。

sentences.en: Modern yo-yoing, there's been technology revolutions.
sentences.zh: 现代悠悠球技术已经发生了革命。

sentences.en: It's gotten super complicated.
sentences.zh: 它变得超级复杂。

sentences.en: It blew up with skateboarding.
sentences.zh: 它随着滑板运动一起爆发了。

sentences.en: There's been really interesting and intricate topological structures you build.
sentences.zh: 其中有一些非常有趣且复杂的拓扑结构。

sentences.en: But I just want you to imagine me being an apparently adult philosophy professor at a dinner party having to tell other people that I've been goddamn yo-yoing in my free time.
sentences.zh: 但我只想让你想象一下，我作为一个成年哲学教授，在晚宴上不得不告诉别人，我在空闲时间一直在玩该死的悠悠球。

sentences.en: People look at me like I've gone nuts and they look at me like I'm making a joke.
sentences.zh: 人们看着我，就像我疯了一样，或者觉得我在开玩笑。

sentences.en: Because trying to explain – I mean I think in any of your – anybody – in any weird obsession you have, right, when you actually get to the reason that's important,
sentences.zh: 因为试图解释——我的意思是，我认为在你的任何——任何人的——任何奇怪的痴迷中，对吧，当你真正触及它重要的原因时，

sentences.en: the reason that really moves you, it's not going to be very accessible to people that aren't deeply in that thing.
sentences.zh: 那个真正打动你的原因，对于那些没有深入其中的人来说，是很难理解的。

sentences.en: T argues that one of the reasons yo-yoing seems like a goof is because it doesn't really have understandable metrics.
sentences.zh: 温特认为，玩悠悠球看起来像个傻瓜的原因之一，是因为它没有真正可理解的指标。

sentences.en: We excuse adults doing childish things if there's a record to beat or a score to measure.
sentences.zh: 如果有一个纪录可以打破或一个分数可以衡量，我们就会原谅成年人做幼稚的事情。

sentences.en: Those things would make yo-yoing comprehensible and therefore would make you understood as a human.
sentences.zh: 那些东西会让玩悠悠球变得可理解，从而让你作为一个人类被理解。

sentences.en: And understood instantly.
sentences.zh: 而且是瞬间被理解。

sentences.en: I think that's – there's not – I mean I think there are a lot of weird things that I love.
sentences.zh: 我认为那是——并不是——我是说我认为我喜欢很多奇怪的东西。

sentences.en: That if someone trusts me and we spend some time together, I can transmit that.
sentences.zh: 如果有人信任我，我们花点时间在一起，我就能传达那种感觉。

sentences.en: But metrics make you comprehensible instantly at scale.
sentences.zh: 但指标能让你在大规模范围内瞬间变得可理解。

sentences.en: Hearing all this, it's easy to get the impression that scoring systems and metrics are more or less evil.
sentences.zh: 听到这些，很容易给人一种印象，即评分系统和指标或多或少是邪恶的。

sentences.en: That although they're alluring in their simplicity, which can help us feel understood, they end up draining the life out of everything we hold dear.
sentences.zh: 尽管它们因其简单性而诱人，能帮助我们感到被理解，但它们最终会耗尽我们所珍视的一切的生命力。

sentences.en: But actually, T would disagree.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，温特并不同意。

sentences.en: He argues that in the right context, scoring systems can also be a way to unlock connection, creativity, and even great joy.
sentences.zh: 他认为在正确的环境下，评分系统也可以成为开启连接、创造力甚至巨大快乐的一种方式。

sentences.en: And the place that this is most readily visible is in gameplay.
sentences.zh: 而这一点最显而易见的地方就是在游戏过程中。

sentences.en: This is the paradox I got obsessed with, right?
sentences.zh: 这就是我沉迷其中的悖论，对吧？

sentences.en: In games, scoring systems are beautiful.
sentences.zh: 在游戏中，评分系统是美丽的。

sentences.en: And then in metrics, scoring systems often seem like they're responsible for the worst part of our lives, for the destruction of education, for the destruction of the arts,
sentences.zh: 而在指标中，评分系统似乎往往是我们生活中最糟糕部分的罪魁祸首，是教育毁灭、艺术毁灭、

sentences.en: for the destruction of the entire environment, ecosystem, and everything that we care about and that's good.
sentences.zh: 整个环境、生态系统以及我们所关心和美好的事物毁灭的根源。

sentences.en: And, like, the thing I was trying to figure out is why scoring systems gave us such delightful play in games and gave us such soul-draining awfulness in metrics.
sentences.zh: 而且，我试图弄清楚的是，为什么评分系统在游戏中给了我们如此美妙的乐趣，而在指标中却给了我们如此令人窒息的痛苦。

sentences.en: Tia and I both love games and the design of games.
sentences.zh: 我和温特都热爱游戏和游戏设计。

sentences.en: And so we got really into talking about the magic of games and why exactly the scoring systems that hurt us in life can make games so rewarding.
sentences.zh: 所以我们深入探讨了游戏的魔力，以及为什么生活中伤害我们的评分系统在游戏中却能让游戏变得如此有意义。

sentences.en: The funny thing about scoring systems is they are kind of little dictators.
sentences.zh: 关于评分系统，有趣的一点是它们就像小独裁者。

sentences.en: They tell you what you're supposed to want and value.
sentences.zh: 它们告诉你你应该想要什么、重视什么。

sentences.en: And that's the weird thing.
sentences.zh: 这就是奇怪的地方。

sentences.en: Scoring systems are little definitions of success and failure.
sentences.zh: 评分系统是关于成功和失败的小定义。

sentences.en: And I think one of the biggest differences is that in games, those definitions are temporary and playful and under your control.
sentences.zh: 我认为最大的区别之一在于，在游戏中，这些定义是暂时的、好玩的，并且在你的控制之下。

sentences.en: And if you don't like it, you can throw it away and you never have to play again.
sentences.zh: 如果你不喜欢，你可以把它扔掉，再也不用玩了。

sentences.en: And in institutions, they're authoritarian.
sentences.zh: 而在机构中，它们是威权主义的。

sentences.en: Like a true philosopher, Tia considers all kinds of things games.
sentences.zh: 像一个真正的哲学家一样，温特把各种各样的事情都视为游戏。

sentences.en: Board games, rock climbing, even fly fishing.
sentences.zh: 棋盘游戏、攀岩，甚至是飞钓。

sentences.en: And something that kept coming up for him in writing this book is the way that in games, scoring systems are an integral part of the fun.
sentences.zh: 在写这本书的过程中，他不断提到的一点是，在游戏中，评分系统是乐趣不可或缺的一部分。

sentences.en: One of the things that got me writing this book was that I had spent a bunch of years trying to explain what games were.
sentences.zh: 促使我写这本书的原因之一是，我花了好几年时间试图解释什么是游戏。

sentences.en: And I ended up saying that there were these beautiful structures that use scoring systems to give us alternate selves, that they gave us alternate desires.
sentences.zh: 最后我得出结论，它们是美丽的结构，利用评分系统赋予我们另一个自我，赋予我们另一种欲望。

sentences.en: And a game just told you, make baskets, collect sheep, get to the top of the rock.
sentences.zh: 游戏只是告诉你：投篮、收集羊、爬到岩石顶端。

sentences.en: And suddenly this thing you might never have cared about before, like getting to the top of some weird boulder.
sentences.zh: 突然间，这件你以前可能从未关心过的事情，比如爬到某块奇怪的巨石顶端，

sentences.en: You're like, I need to do it.
sentences.zh: 你会觉得：我必须做到。

sentences.en: And then suddenly this whole new activity unlocks.
sentences.zh: 然后突然间，一种全新的活动被解锁了。

sentences.en: Now, I love playing games with my kids.
sentences.zh: 现在，我喜欢和我的孩子们玩游戏。

sentences.en: And since my kids are all over the country now, we plan game nights like months in advance.
sentences.zh: 由于我的孩子们现在分散在全国各地，我们提前几个月计划游戏之夜。

sentences.en: And I am just competitive enough inside of a game to make it fun.
sentences.zh: 在游戏中，我的好胜心足以让它变得有趣。

sentences.en: I am not trying to lose.
sentences.zh: 我不是为了输而玩。

sentences.en: I am definitely trying to win.
sentences.zh: 我绝对是为了赢。

sentences.en: But I have to say, at the end of the night, or even at the end of any round of game, I cannot tell you who won that game.
sentences.zh: 但我必须说，在夜晚结束时，甚至在任何一轮游戏结束时，我都无法告诉你谁赢了那场游戏。

sentences.en: I cannot imagine caring about a game's outcome.
sentences.zh: 我无法想象怎么会有人在意一场游戏的结果。

sentences.en: I've never been able to describe this to people.
sentences.zh: 我一直无法向别人描述这种感觉。

sentences.en: But Tia explained it to me that there are two types of play.
sentences.zh: 但蒂亚（Tia）向我解释说，游戏有两种类型。

sentences.en: Striving play and achievement play.
sentences.zh: 奋斗型游戏和成就型游戏。

sentences.en: Achievement play is caring about winning, right?
sentences.zh: 成就型游戏就是那种在意输赢的游戏，对吧？

sentences.en: Achievement play is caring about, it's playing because you actually want to win.
sentences.zh: 成就型游戏在意的是……玩游戏是因为你真的想赢。

sentences.en: Striving play is when you temporarily get yourself to want to win in order to experience the struggle.
sentences.zh: 奋斗型游戏是指你暂时让自己想要获胜，以便去体验那种奋斗的过程。

sentences.en: So the difference between the two is not about how intense you are about trying to win.
sentences.zh: 所以两者的区别不在于你有多想赢。

sentences.en: You can be a striving player and be trying really intensely.
sentences.zh: 你完全可以作为一个奋斗型玩家，并且非常投入地去争取胜利。

sentences.en: The difference is the striving play values the experience, not if they win, but if the struggle was interesting.
sentences.zh: 区别在于，奋斗型玩家看重的是体验，不是赢不赢，而是奋斗的过程是否有意思。

sentences.en: I am 100% a striver.
sentences.zh: 我百分之百是个奋斗型玩家。

sentences.en: But I still get wrapped up in the goal and drama of the game when I'm inside that game.
sentences.zh: 但当我身处游戏之中时，我还是会不由自主地陷入游戏的目标和戏剧性中。

sentences.en: So my family plays this game called Wingspan.
sentences.zh: 我们家经常玩一款叫《展翅翱翔》（Wingspan）的游戏。

sentences.en: And it's a beautiful little game that is more intuitive than all the little pieces and dense rules would have you to believe.
sentences.zh: 那是一款精美的小游戏，比它那些繁杂的配件和密集的规则看起来要直观得多。

sentences.en: But my stepdaughter hates this game.
sentences.zh: 但我继女讨厌这个游戏。

sentences.en: She hates Wingspan.
sentences.zh: 她讨厌《展翅翱翔》。

sentences.en: Because I swear a lot when I play this game.
sentences.zh: 因为我玩这个游戏时总是骂脏话。

sentences.en: There are often these scenarios when I need a certain card pull or a roll of the dice to make a very long planned strategy pay off.
sentences.zh: 经常会出现这种情况：我需要抽到某张特定的牌或者掷出特定的点数，才能让筹划已久的策略奏效。

sentences.en: And I often don't get that card that I want.
sentences.zh: 而我往往抽不到想要的牌。

sentences.en: And hence the swearing.
sentences.zh: 于是我就开始骂人。

sentences.en: Since I am a very calm, non-volatile presence in her life, she hates hearing me swear.
sentences.zh: 因为我在她生活中一直是个非常冷静、情绪稳定的人，所以她很讨厌听到我骂人。

sentences.en: And this game just brings it out of me more than moSt.
sentences.zh: 而这个游戏比其他任何东西都更能激发出我这一面。

sentences.en: I don't know why.
sentences.zh: 我也不知道为什么。

sentences.en: But it turns out this freedom to swear, to connive and compete, is actually part of the magic of games.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，这种骂人、耍心机和竞争的自由，其实正是游戏魔力的一部分。

sentences.en: They give us this healthy arena for feelings that aren't so healthy in the real world.
sentences.zh: 它们为我们在现实世界中不太健康的情绪提供了一个健康的宣泄场所。

sentences.en: One of the interesting things about games is they're a place where we're released to do something like that.
sentences.zh: 游戏有趣的地方之一在于，它们是一个让我们被允许去做这类事情的地方。

sentences.en: Jan Husinga, an anthropologist who studied games in the early 20th century.
sentences.zh: 扬·赫伊津哈（Jan Huizinga），一位在20世纪初研究游戏的人类学家。

sentences.en: One of the first great scholars of play.
sentences.zh: 他是最早期的伟大游戏学者之一。

sentences.en: He said that what makes games and play distinctive is that they occur in a magic circle where the meanings of what you do are screened off from ordinary life.
sentences.zh: 他说，游戏和玩耍的独特之处在于，它们发生在一个“魔圈”里，在这里，你所作所为的意义与日常生活是隔绝开来的。

sentences.en: So what this means is like, you know, if we're close friends and then we're playing basketball against each other and you block my pass,
sentences.zh: 这意味着，比如我们是好朋友，然后我们在打篮球对抗，你盖了我的帽，

sentences.en: I'm not going to come up after you afterwards and be like, how could you do that to me?
sentences.zh: 我事后不会跑去质问你：你怎么能那样对我？

sentences.en: You wound me, my friend.
sentences.zh: 朋友，你伤害了我。

sentences.en: I thought we were close.
sentences.zh: 我以为我们关系很好。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: And because the meanings are screened off in that way, because the points, I mean, part of the point is the points are valueless.
sentences.zh: 正因为意义是以这种方式被隔绝的，正因为得分——我的意思是，得分本身其实毫无价值。

sentences.en: And we know that galactically, even if in the game we're really into it, which makes us release to be like, I try so hard in my life to be a nice person and to be a kind person.
sentences.zh: 我们从宏观上知道这一点，即使在游戏中我们非常投入，这让我们得以释放——我在生活中努力做一个好人、一个善良的人。

sentences.en: But there's a part of my brain that is a complete Machiavellian asshole.
sentences.zh: 但我大脑中有一部分是一个彻头彻尾的马基雅维利式的混蛋。

sentences.en: And I have to keep that under wraps most of the time.
sentences.zh: 大多数时候我必须把它藏起来。

sentences.en: I don't get to do that.
sentences.zh: 我没机会表现出来。

sentences.en: And in the game environment, because it's so screened off from the rest of life in just this simple way, I can do that.
sentences.zh: 而在游戏环境中，因为它以这种简单的方式与生活的其余部分隔绝开来，我就可以那样做。

sentences.en: It is part of the contract of gaming that when I play with my family or my friends, we can go all out.
sentences.zh: 游戏契约的一部分就是，当我与家人或朋友玩游戏时，我们可以全力以赴。

sentences.en: We can lie to each other.
sentences.zh: 我们可以互相撒谎。

sentences.en: We can, you know, manipulate.
sentences.zh: 我们可以，你知道，操纵局势。

sentences.en: We can deceive each other.
sentences.zh: 我们可以互相欺骗。

sentences.en: We can look for each other's weaknesses and destroy each other because we know that the gaming environment has designed to turn that into an interesting struggle.
sentences.zh: 我们可以寻找对方的弱点并摧毁对方，因为我们知道游戏环境的设计初衷就是将其转化为一场有趣的斗争。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: A great example that you give of striving play is fly fishing, which is a thing I also, I don't, I love it.
sentences.zh: 你提到的奋斗型游戏的一个绝佳例子是飞蝇钓，这也是我……我并不，我热爱它。

sentences.en: Like I have a fly fishing kit.
sentences.zh: 我有全套飞蝇钓装备。

sentences.en: I went to a fly fishing class.
sentences.zh: 我还去上过飞蝇钓课程。

sentences.en: I haven't sort of gotten off my ass to do fly fishing, but I just admire everything about it.
sentences.zh: 我还没怎么真正动身去钓过，但我就是欣赏它的一切。

sentences.en: And the more I learned about it, the more I admired it.
sentences.zh: 我了解得越多，就越欣赏它。

sentences.en: Could you talk about the fly fishing in terms of striving play?
sentences.zh: 你能从奋斗型游戏的角度谈谈飞蝇钓吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 可以。

sentences.en: Fly fishing is really interesting to me.
sentences.zh: 飞蝇钓对我来说真的很有趣。

sentences.en: Um, so I am in Utah and in Utah, there are a lot of dudes with this very obsessive interest in fly fishing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我在犹他州，在犹他州，有很多家伙对飞蝇钓有着非常痴迷的兴趣。

sentences.en: So fly fishing, I thought was about, I don't know what it was.
sentences.zh: 所以我原以为飞蝇钓是关于……我不知道它是什么。

sentences.en: I thought it was just like about having fancy gear and about like repeatedly casting and casting and casting.
sentences.zh: 我以为它只是关于拥有昂贵的装备，关于反复地抛投、抛投、再抛投。

sentences.en: And what I found about fly fishing was, what's interesting is that it's actually a sport about attention.
sentences.zh: 而我发现飞蝇钓有趣的地方在于，它实际上是一项关于专注力的运动。

sentences.en: So what you're doing if you're fly fishing, especially in the style I like, which is dry fly fishing,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你在进行飞蝇钓，特别是我喜欢的这种风格——干式飞蝇钓，

sentences.en: which is where you're trying to get a fish to swim up and eat a bug off the surface.
sentences.zh: 也就是你试图引诱鱼游上来吃掉水面上的虫子，

sentences.en: What you're often doing is walking along a river, in a river,
sentences.zh: 你通常是在河边走，或者在河里走，

sentences.en: looking for either actually being able to see a trout rising or being able to see the quality of water where a trout is likely to be under the water.
sentences.zh: 寻找那些真正能看到的跃起的鳟鱼，或者观察水质，判断鳟鱼可能潜伏在水下的位置。

sentences.en: And then you have to figure out what kind of bugs it's feeding, which means you have to be really attentive to what is hatching in the air, which can change every 20 minutes.
sentences.zh: 然后你必须弄清楚它在吃哪种虫子，这意味着你必须非常关注空气中正在孵化的昆虫，而这每20分钟就会变一次。

sentences.en: And so what the game does is it, it forces you to hyper focus on small, subtle visual details across a huge ecological landscape.
sentences.zh: 所以这个游戏所做的，就是强迫你在广阔的生态景观中，对微小、细微的视觉细节进行高度聚焦。

sentences.en: And one of the things I found interesting is if I go to a river without the fly fishing game, I look at the river for like a minute and then I'm bored and I look away.
sentences.zh: 我发现有趣的一点是，如果我不带这个“飞蝇钓游戏”去河边，我盯着河看一分钟就会觉得无聊，然后就移开视线了。

sentences.en: If you give me the game, then I can zero in on the surface of the water and have focus for hours.
sentences.zh: 但如果你给我这个游戏，我就能锁定水面，并保持专注好几个小时。

sentences.en: And it's really like two or three hours into focusing intensely on a river that I achieve like, I don't know,
sentences.zh: 在高度专注地盯着河面两三个小时后，我真的会达到一种……我不知道，

sentences.en: like these like weird altered mental states of complete like zend out brain water have flowed together.
sentences.zh: 就像那种奇怪的、改变了的精神状态，完全像禅定一样，大脑和水流融为一体。

sentences.en: But I think it's really funky.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这真的很奇妙。

sentences.en: Like the game is a support structure for that kind of attention.
sentences.zh: 游戏是这种专注力的支撑结构。

sentences.en: It's very hard to get there on your own.
sentences.zh: 靠自己很难达到那种境界。

sentences.en: When I try seated meditation, I can't get there.
sentences.zh: 当我尝试静坐冥想时，我做不到。

sentences.en: If someone's like, pay attention to the river until your mind empties and merges to the river, I'd be like, I have no idea how to do that.
sentences.zh: 如果有人说，盯着河看，直到你的心空无一物并融入河流，我会说，我根本不知道该怎么做。

sentences.en: What?
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.en: But if someone's like, look for trout and then notice what insects are and then try to caSt.
sentences.zh: 但如果有人说，寻找鳟鱼，然后注意昆虫是什么，然后尝试抛投。

sentences.en: Then that's like a little tangible thread that I can crawl my way into this subtle, subtle mental state.
sentences.zh: 那就像是一根有形的细线，我可以顺着它爬进这种微妙、微妙的精神状态中。

sentences.en: One of the interesting things about games is you don't need to understand them for them to act on you, right?
sentences.zh: 游戏有趣的地方之一在于，你不需要理解它们，它们就能对你产生作用，对吧？

sentences.en: Like what a game is, is it tells you to do something and it gives you some constraints.
sentences.zh: 游戏就是告诉你去做某事，并给你一些限制。

sentences.en: And you're like, I don't know, what's that for?
sentences.zh: 你会想，我不知道，这有什么意义？

sentences.en: And you just try it.
sentences.zh: 然后你就试着去做。

sentences.en: Do it, yeah.
sentences.zh: 去做吧，没错。

sentences.en: And then suddenly you have these discoveries of, I see this all the time.
sentences.zh: 然后突然间你就有了一些发现，我经常看到这种情况。

sentences.en: Like people playing Dungeons and Dragons for the first time.
sentences.zh: 比如第一次玩《龙与地下城》的人。

sentences.en: Playing like a social communication party game like The Mind for the first time.
sentences.zh: 第一次玩像《心灵同步》（The Mind）这种社交沟通派对游戏的人。

sentences.en: Trying rock climbing for the first time.
sentences.zh: 第一次尝试攀岩的人。

sentences.en: They don't know what it's for.
sentences.zh: 他们不知道这有什么意义。

sentences.en: They don't know the reasons why anyone would do it.
sentences.zh: 他们不知道为什么会有人做这些事。

sentences.en: Someone talks to them to do it.
sentences.zh: 有人告诉他们去做。

sentences.en: But they try it and the rules kind of force them into an intentional posture of looking at the world and seeking out, looking for holes in the rock,
sentences.zh: 但他们尝试了，规则强迫他们进入一种有意识的姿态，去观察世界，去寻找岩石上的孔洞，

sentences.en: looking for little bugs in the air.
sentences.zh: 去寻找空气中的小虫子。

sentences.en: And suddenly they're doing that.
sentences.zh: 突然间，他们就在做这些事了。

sentences.en: And then something happens to their mind and body.
sentences.zh: 然后他们的身心发生了一些变化。

sentences.en: And they find that there's some like weird new radiant kind of beauty that they hadn't known about and that they couldn't have chased directly.
sentences.zh: 他们发现了一种奇怪的、新的、灿烂的美，那是他们以前不知道的，也是他们无法直接追求到的。

sentences.en: This is the magic of games.
sentences.zh: 这就是游戏的魔力。

sentences.en: More with T-Win after this.
sentences.zh: 稍后继续与T-Win的对话。

sentences.en: We're back with C.T.
sentences.zh: 我们回到与C.T.的对话。

sentences.en: Winn.
sentences.zh: 温（Winn）。

sentences.en: I'm really interested in how to use metrics for good because objective measures and transparencies are key components to, you know, good government, progressive era politics.
sentences.zh: 我非常关心如何利用指标来造福社会，因为客观的衡量标准和透明度是良好政府和进步时代政治的关键组成部分。

sentences.en: And, you know, we've talked about Robert Moses a lot on the show.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我们在节目中谈论过很多次罗伯特·摩西（Robert Moses）。

sentences.en: And before he became the villain of the power broker, he was championing civil service reform.
sentences.zh: 在他成为《权力掮客》（The Power Broker）中的反派之前，他曾是公务员制度改革的倡导者。

sentences.en: And that's all about measuring achievement, taking tests and making sure people got jobs because they deserve them and not because they were someone's nephew.
sentences.zh: 那一切都是关于衡量成就、参加考试，并确保人们得到工作是因为他们有能力，而不是因为他们是谁的侄子。

sentences.en: So how do we use scores and scoring systems in an effective way to make the world a better place and have them not dominate our lives in a bad way?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们该如何有效地利用分数和评分系统来让世界变得更美好，同时又不让它们以糟糕的方式主宰我们的生活呢？

sentences.en: One of the most famous cases, I think, is the quantification of policing in New York police districts.
sentences.zh: 我认为最著名的案例之一，就是纽约警察局辖区的警务量化。

sentences.en: So in the early days, people said, like, look, all these police districts say that they're doing well.
sentences.zh: 在早期，人们说，看，所有这些警察辖区都说他们做得很好。

sentences.en: We can't tell if they're doing well.
sentences.zh: 我们无法判断他们是否真的做得好。

sentences.en: So we're going to put clear metrics about what we can measure, which is how many cases get closed, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我们要制定明确的指标来衡量我们可以测量的东西，也就是结案率，对吧？

sentences.en: How many arrests do we make?
sentences.zh: 我们逮捕了多少人？

sentences.en: And what happened was in the first bunch of years, it worked great.
sentences.zh: 结果在最初的几年里，效果非常好。

sentences.en: It detected all kinds of corruption, all kinds of bias, and it forced people to rid it, get that out of the system.
sentences.zh: 它检测出了各种腐败和偏见，并迫使人们将其从系统中清除。

sentences.en: And then after a little while, I think it's a story that a lot of people know, that I learned from the TV show The Wire.
sentences.zh: 然后过了一段时间，我想这是一个很多人都知道的故事，我是从电视剧《火线》（The Wire）里学到的。

sentences.en: Same.
sentences.zh: 我也是。

sentences.en: People started, like, gaming those metrics, right?
sentences.zh: 人们开始玩弄这些指标，对吧？

sentences.en: You can game those metrics easily.
sentences.zh: 你可以很容易地操纵这些指标。

sentences.en: One way to make your case closure rate look good is to discourage people from reporting crimes, right?
sentences.zh: 让结案率看起来好看的一种方法是劝阻人们报案，对吧？

sentences.en: One way to up your case closure rate is speeding tickets because you open the case and you close it at the same time.
sentences.zh: 提高结案率的另一种方法是开超速罚单，因为你立案的同时也就结案了。

sentences.en: So in the beginning, it gets rid of corruption and bias because the metrics are so brute that everyone can understand them.
sentences.zh: 所以起初，它消除了腐败和偏见，因为指标非常粗糙，每个人都能理解。

sentences.en: And after a period of time, they seem to drain what's genuinely valuable from the system because they point people at something that's very easily and mechanically checkable.
sentences.zh: 但过了一段时间，它们似乎耗尽了系统中真正有价值的东西，因为它们引导人们去关注那些非常容易且机械化检查的东西。

sentences.en: And measurable.
sentences.zh: 以及可衡量的东西。

sentences.en: So in T's Police and Example, metrics start out as being helpful and in service of offering transparency to the public.
sentences.zh: 所以在T的警察案例中，指标起初是有帮助的，旨在为公众提供透明度。

sentences.en: But eventually, they end up being counterproductive and sometimes even dangerous.
sentences.zh: 但最终，它们变得适得其反，有时甚至很危险。

sentences.en: And he told me that a similar dynamic can play out with population-wide statistics, where you're trying to get a sense of trends on a really big scale.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，类似的动态也可能发生在人口统计数据中，当你试图在大规模尺度上把握趋势时。

sentences.en: What makes metrics work well is that they work at scale really faSt.
sentences.zh: 指标之所以有效，是因为它们能非常快地在大规模尺度上运作。

sentences.en: So they're really good for us to coordinate around for vast social efforts.
sentences.zh: 所以它们非常适合我们围绕大规模社会努力进行协调。

sentences.en: So if you're going to coordinate the entire world around reducing CO2 emissions or increasing vaccination rates, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你要协调全世界来减少二氧化碳排放或提高疫苗接种率，对吧？

sentences.en: That's a really simple thing.
sentences.zh: 那是一件非常简单的事情。

sentences.en: And when we count it in the same way, we can cooperate really easily.
sentences.zh: 当我们以同样的方式计算它时，我们就能非常容易地合作。

sentences.en: The cost is there are only certain kinds of things that we all measure in the same way and count in the same way that we can coordinate around.
sentences.zh: 代价是，只有某些我们都能以相同方式衡量和计算的事物，我们才能围绕它们进行协调。

sentences.en: So here's – that suggests another answer, which is that some kinds of targets are naturally stable at scale and easy for everyone to count at scale.
sentences.zh: 所以这暗示了另一个答案，那就是某些类型的目标在规模上是自然稳定的，并且每个人在规模上都很容易计算。

sentences.en: And it's easier to get good metrics of that.
sentences.zh: 而且更容易获得这些指标的良好数据。

sentences.en: So I'll give you an example.
sentences.zh: 我给你举个例子。

sentences.en: It's much easier to get a good metric for lifespan and mortality rate than it is to get a metric for mental health.
sentences.zh: 获得寿命和死亡率的良好指标，要比获得心理健康的指标容易得多。

sentences.en: Everyone counts lifespan and deaths in the same way.
sentences.zh: 每个人都以同样的方式计算寿命和死亡人数。

sentences.en: These other things aren't counted in the same way.
sentences.zh: 而其他这些东西并没有以同样的方式计算。

sentences.en: So it is appropriate in those cases because the kind of thing that's being targeted is the kind of thing that's stable at scale.
sentences.zh: 因此，在这些情况下是合适的，因为被瞄准的目标类型是在规模上稳定的。

sentences.en: But the worry, the price is that we tend to socially over-attend to those qualities, that we over-attend to lifespan and mortality rate instead of mental well-being, flourishing,
sentences.zh: 但令人担忧的代价是，我们倾向于在社会层面上过度关注这些品质，我们过度关注寿命和死亡率，而不是心理健康、繁荣、

sentences.en: community flourishing, social relationships.
sentences.zh: 社区繁荣和社交关系。

sentences.en: So I guess the point I'm wondering is like what do we do with all this?
sentences.zh: 所以我猜我想知道的是，我们该如何处理这一切？

sentences.en: Like how do we live and thrive in a world where we have no choice but to engage with these metrics in so many areas in our lives?
sentences.zh: 我们如何在这样一个世界中生活和茁壮成长，在这个世界里，我们别无选择，只能在生活的许多领域与这些指标打交道？

sentences.en: Yeah, so I would like to give you the peppy answer of like just grit up and play with the institutions in your lives.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以我很想给你一个充满活力的回答，比如“振作起来，去适应你生活中的制度”。

sentences.en: But that's not – I mean I think one of the things we know is that if you quit a game, nothing happens.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是……我的意思是，我认为我们知道的一件事是，如果你退出一个游戏，什么都不会发生。

sentences.en: And if you quit your KPIs or your other metrics at your work, you get fired and then you starve and then your family died.
sentences.zh: 但如果你退出了工作中的KPI或其他指标，你就会被解雇，然后挨饿，然后你的家庭就会破碎。

sentences.en: It's not the same.
sentences.zh: 这不一样。

sentences.en: But I think you can still – there are a few things you can do.
sentences.zh: 但我认为你仍然可以……有几件事你可以做。

sentences.en: One thing you can do is at least have some ironic distance.
sentences.zh: 你可以做的一件事是至少保持某种反讽的距离。

sentences.en: I think there's a huge difference between someone thinking my goal in life is to have the most subscribers versus my goal is to communicate and have all these other things.
sentences.zh: 我认为一个人认为“我的人生目标是拥有最多的订阅者”与“我的目标是交流并拥有所有这些其他东西”之间有巨大的区别。

sentences.en: And I need subscribers to do it but I'm willing to trade off against it, right?
sentences.zh: 我需要订阅者来做到这一点，但我愿意为此做出权衡，对吧？

sentences.en: That's one thing.
sentences.zh: 这是一件事。

sentences.en: The last thing T told me about though was my favorite approach to living in a world defined by metrics without letting them define you.
sentences.zh: 不过，T告诉我的最后一件事是我最喜欢的方法，即如何在由指标定义的世界中生活，而不让它们定义你。

sentences.en: He talked about finding little places in your life where you can choose to create or define your own metrics, which lets you design the game you actually want to be playing.
sentences.zh: 他谈到了在生活中找到一些小地方，在那里你可以选择创造或定义自己的指标，这让你能够设计出你真正想玩的游戏。

sentences.en: I complained about metrics forever and then I realized I was in charge of a huge one for my students.
sentences.zh: 我抱怨了指标很久，然后我意识到我负责为我的学生制定一个巨大的指标。

sentences.en: My grading system for my students is a scoring system that I have – I am an authority and I was just being an unthinking authoritarian.
sentences.zh: 我给学生打分用的是一套我自己的评分系统——我身为权威，却表现得像个不假思索的独裁者。

sentences.en: And so this might amuse you but the last two years as I've been thinking about this,
sentences.zh: 所以，这件事可能会让你觉得好笑，过去两年里我一直在思考这个问题，

sentences.en: I decided that I had not realized the degree to which as I complained about the tyranny of metrics, I was turning around and imposing it on my students.
sentences.zh: 我意识到，我一边抱怨指标的暴政，一边却转过身来把它强加给我的学生，而我之前竟然毫无察觉。

sentences.en: And so I've been trying an experiment.
sentences.zh: 于是，我一直在做一个实验。

sentences.en: I have been letting my students design their own scoring system.
sentences.zh: 我让学生们自己设计他们的评分系统。

sentences.en: So what I've been doing in my tech and design ethics class is walking in and saying none of us have any clue what to do about ChatGPT in the classroom.
sentences.zh: 我在科技与设计伦理课上所做的，就是走进教室，告诉大家我们谁也不知道该如何应对课堂上的 ChatGPT。

sentences.en: And so as an exercise in the class, we will talk about the philosophy of education, AI, and democracy.
sentences.zh: 因此，作为课堂练习，我们将讨论教育哲学、人工智能和民主。

sentences.en: And then they will democratically design their own grading system and assignments for the class.
sentences.zh: 然后，他们将以民主的方式为这门课设计自己的评分系统和作业。

sentences.en: And that's something I could have done all along and I didn't realize it.
sentences.zh: 这其实是我一直都能做到的事，但我之前没意识到。

sentences.en: How did that go?
sentences.zh: 效果如何？

sentences.en: Amazing.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Unbelievable.
sentences.zh: 简直不可思议。

sentences.en: Let me tell you.
sentences.zh: 让我告诉你。

sentences.en: First of all, process over outcome.
sentences.zh: 首先，过程重于结果。

sentences.en: The grading system they designed was actually quite good.
sentences.zh: 他们设计的评分系统其实相当不错。

sentences.en: But the process of coming up with it was more valuable than any other assignment I've ever done.
sentences.zh: 但制定这个系统的过程，比我布置过的任何其他作业都更有价值。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: They get so invested and they ended up talking seriously about what an education was for, what a grading system was for, what the use of AI was for, what all of it meant.
sentences.zh: 他们投入了极大的热情，最终开始认真讨论教育的目的是什么、评分系统的目的是什么、人工智能的用途是什么，以及这一切意味着什么。

sentences.en: They took it super seriously.
sentences.zh: 他们非常认真地对待这件事。

sentences.en: And I think, among other things, it taught them systems thinking.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，除此以外，这还教会了他们系统性思维。

sentences.en: They started having to think about how the design of a grading system changed an education and how you get good and bad design.
sentences.zh: 他们开始思考评分系统的设计如何改变教育，以及如何区分好的设计和坏的设计。

sentences.en: And I think part of what I was trying to do was get students to see what you're trying to get people to see,
sentences.zh: 我想我试图做的一部分工作，就是让学生们看到你试图让人们看到的东西，

sentences.en: which is that all these quiet design decisions in the background totally change how people interact.
sentences.zh: 那就是所有这些背景中默默存在的设计决策，彻底改变了人们的互动方式。

sentences.en: Like, who cares in some sense?
sentences.zh: 比如，从某种意义上说，谁在乎呢？

sentences.en: I mean, they did come up with a good grading system,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们确实想出了一个好的评分系统，

sentences.en: but I kind of don't care if they did because the process of coming up with it actually got me what I wanted from the class in the first place.
sentences.zh: 但我其实并不在乎他们是否做到了，因为制定这个系统的过程，实际上已经让我达成了这门课最初的目标。

sentences.en: I had just a great time talking with you.
sentences.zh: 和你聊天非常愉快。

sentences.en: I love the book, The Score.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢《分数》这本书。

sentences.en: I just – I had so much fun reading it and I had so much fun sort of like looking at it and using it to decode my life and my choices.
sentences.zh: 我读得非常开心，在阅读它并用它来解读我的生活和选择时，我也感到非常快乐。

sentences.en: I really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我真的很感激。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: We'll see you next time.
sentences.zh: 我们下次再见。
